resources.string: Switches the in-app display language. The default (System) follows the phone language setting. Picking 日本語 or English pins that language regardless of the phone. In English, untranslated parts remain in Japanese (more translation coming), and the Japanese flick keyboard is hidden.
Login shell (applies from the next session)

Prints the current time dimmed at the right edge of the line, so scrolling back shows when each command was typed. It does not count the terminal width, so rotating or splitting the screen never misaligns it.
What gets written to %1$s (edit it here to fine-tune)
Written to %1$s. New tabs pick it up.
Removed from %1$s. New tabs go back to the default.

Pick a sample to fill the box, edit it if you like, then press Apply to write it into the config file of the shell you picked. Only the part between the z2term markers is written, so anything you wrote yourself stays. Opening the file from the terminal with vi shows the same thing.
Adds a numbers-only face (a keypad) to the built-in keyboard, so the switch key cycles through 12 as well. Turn it off and the cycle is あ → A → あ as before
Show a show/hide bar above the keyboard. When off, double-tap the ⌨ button to toggle.

Add your own words from a file, one word per line. Both "reading /candidate1/candidate2/" (SKK format) and "reading<TAB>word<TAB>part-of-speech" (what IME dictionary tools export) are read. Lines starting with ; or # are comments. UTF-8 and EUC-JP are both read. Only lines whose reading is hiragana are imported.
That file is too large (8MB limit)
No words could be read. Check that each line looks like "reading /candidate/" or tab-separated "reading<TAB>word", and that readings are hiragana
Special key bar (with the OS keyboard)
While the OS keyboard is selected, show ESC, TAB, CTRL and arrow keys above it. Turn off to hide the bar (the built-in keyboard is unaffected).
GUI magnification (applies from next GUI start)
ON: play sound from GUI apps on this device. PulseAudio is installed into the Linux side on first use (downloads a few MB). OFF: no audio, no extra packages.
For CJK locales (works for PowerLine glyphs etc.)
Tap to choose which buttons appear in the terminal top bar. To reorder, long-press a button on the terminal screen and drag left/right.
Hidden from the toolbar, so toggle it here
ON: prompt before downloading a distro or GUI package. OFF: download without confirmation.
ON: the OS is less likely to kill the session and its running processes in the background. Turning OFF opens system settings (Android does not allow apps to re-enable optimization directly).

Android 12/13 may kill the \"phantom processes\" that proot spawns. This cannot be changed inside the app — run the following from a PC via adb, then reboot the device. Android 14+ is usually relaxed already.

Don\'t hold WakeLock/WifiLock — saves battery, but while the screen is off automation reacts more slowly and incoming connections may be delayed or dropped. It applies to both resident servers and 🔒 background keep-alive (servers pick it up on their next start). While neither of those is running, changing this setting changes nothing.
Where to place the on-screen keyboard when the screen is in landscape. Portrait always uses Bottom.
Portrait and landscape heights are remembered separately and switch automatically with the screen orientation.
Delete data for OS images you don\'t use to free up space. Deleting removes all packages, settings and files inside that OS.
No OS data to delete yet.
All packages, settings and files inside %1$s will be erased. This cannot be undone. Delete anyway?
A process is still running in this tab. Closing it will terminate the running program. Close anyway?

This returns the app to the state it had when first opened. Only a single terminal tab is left open (other terminal tabs and GUI tabs are closed), and that terminal goes back to its initial state: running programs are terminated and the screen and scrollback are cleared.\n\nSaved servers, settings, snippets and the OS itself (installed packages and your files) are not affected.

This is stronger than Reset terminal. It stops resident servers, system event capture, every terminal and GUI session, and the app’s foreground service, then removes the app task.\n\nSettings, server definitions, installed packages and your files are not deleted. Detection configured in settings resumes the next time you open the app.

Delete the following re-downloadable caches (%1$s total):
%2$s

Installed packages, settings and your files are not affected.
No cache to clear. Package and build caches inside the OS, plus the app download cache, are all empty.

Theme, font, keyboard, execution engine (returns to the default z2root), saved servers, unlocked hidden features and everything else return to their default values. This cannot be undone.\n\nThe OS itself (installed packages and your files) is not affected.
z2root is our own no-root ptrace engine. chroot runs natively as real root and needs a rooted device. New tabs use the selected engine.
Records every z2root syscall into z2root_trace.log.
⚠ For development/diagnostics only. Turning it on makes the log grow huge and quickly fills device storage. Keep it OFF in normal use.
Engine selector unlocked. Pick the engine below.
Engine diagnostics hidden, reset to z2root.
Root unlocked — chroot is now available too.
Root was not granted. If no prompt appears, set Z2Term to "Grant" in your root manager (e.g. Magisk) and tap this button again (Magisk remembers a "Deny" and won\'t prompt again).
Root works but the chroot test failed (possibly SELinux/rootfs): %1$s

chroot appears once you grant root on a rooted device. Re-check with the button below. After a "Deny" the prompt stops appearing, so set Z2Term back to "Grant" in your root manager (e.g. Magisk) first.

plurals.name: settings_root_unlock_countdown
plurals.item: %1$d more tap to toggle the engine selector
%1$d more taps to toggle the engine selector

resources.string: ⚠️ z2root binary not found — run scripts/build-z2root.sh and rebuild. Falling back to Android sh.
Falling back to Android sh mode.
Check network and URL. To revert to Alpine, switch distro in settings.
Shows license texts, copyrights, and corresponding-source URLs in one place.
Bundled OSS licenses and corresponding source URLs. Tap to view the full text.
(The full text for this license is not bundled. SPDX: %1$s\nSee the official text at https://spdx.org/licenses/%1$s.html.)
%1$s will be wiped (rootfs and any downloaded data) and re-fetched from scratch%2$s. Wi-Fi recommended. Continue?
%1$s will be downloaded for the first time%2$s. Wi-Fi recommended. Continue?
Turn ON and pick an OS to wipe its rootfs and downloaded data and reinstall from scratch (recovery for stuck DL/extraction).
Alpine is bundled. Ubuntu / Arch / Kali are downloaded on first switch or clean install (Wi-Fi recommended).
The install screen is up on the device — approve it to finish.
Allow "Install unknown apps" for z2term first, or the install screen never appears.
This build came from a store (F-Droid / Play). Update it there.
That release has no .apk attached — use the release page.
Off: the downloaded file is deleted once the update goes through (and on the next start).
Empty keeps it inside the app, where no other app can see it. e.g. /sdcard/Download
Forwards stay alive even after the SSH tab is closed (runs alongside resident servers). The host key must already be trusted — connect once from the SSH tab first.
⚠ Includes a -R forward: while this runs, the remote side can reach into this device. Forwards stay alive after the SSH tab is closed. The host key must already be trusted.
let the remote reach this device
No history yet. Commands you run in the terminal appear here.
…and %1$d more — narrow the filter to reach them.
Tap a command to put it on the input line. It is inserted, never run.
No history yet. Copies are captured automatically.

▸ Tap a row → pasted into the terminal
▸ Synced with the system clipboard (captured on copy / when the app comes to the foreground)
▸ Rows marked 🔒 disappear after 30 seconds (passwords and the like)
▸ ✕ delete
🔒 Sensitive copy — clears itself after 30 seconds
No entries. Tap "+ New" to add a command.
▸ Tap a row → inserted into the terminal (no Enter)\n▸ Hold ≡ and drag up/down to reorder\n▸ ✎ edit / ✕ delete
Label (if empty, the first part of the command is shown)
No profiles. Tap "+ New" to add one.
init command (run automatically on connect, optional)
None. Tap "+ Add" to create localhost:N → remote:M.
The host key for %1$s is not in known_hosts.
Confirm this is a trusted host.\nA man-in-the-middle attack (MITM) is possible.
\n(fails if the directory is not empty)
This app itself (terminal UI, session/SSH/SFTP, settings)
Create one theme of your own. The chosen background / foreground / accent etc. apply to the whole app.
⚠ %1$s is not installed for this distro. Until it is installed it has no effect; the launcher falls back to the default shell → /bin/sh (e.g. apk add zsh / apt install zsh).
Shells that are not installed fall back automatically. They become effective once you install them in the distro.
When ON, mount physical SD volumes (/storage/XXXX-XXXX) inside the terminal as /sdcard_ext. Takes effect on the next session restart.
No external storage detected. Insert an SD card or grant All Files Access in system settings.
Turn ON to detect external paths.
When ON, bind Android\'s /system and /apex inside PRoot/chroot so aarch64 ELFs (e.g. aapt2) can run. Takes effect on the next restart.
⚠ This makes Android system directories visible inside the terminal. Understand the security implications before enabling.

When ON, allow Kitty graphics t=f/t=t/t=s payloads to read files inside the active rootfs. OFF (default) discards all such requests. Required for some image viewer TUIs that send a path instead of base64.
⚠ Lets TUIs trigger reads of any file under the active distro rootfs. Off by default — only enable for trusted sessions.
SGR mouse output (convert touch to mouse events)

When ON, taps are translated to TUI mouse events (SGR `?1006`). Required for some TUIs (calendar, file managers, multi-pane focus switching). Single tap = left click, long press = right click, one-finger drag = mouse motion. When OFF (default), taps are used by Z2Term itself (focus / text selection / scrolling). Two-finger swipe → wheel works the same regardless of this toggle.
⚠ When enabled, one-finger text selection and long-press menus are routed to the TUI. On screens that do not enable mouse capture (e.g. bash, less) taps still drive Z2Term as before.
Turn ON and open the GUI tab to reinstall the GUI-display packages (cache and all) — recovery for stuck DL/extraction. The check clears automatically on launch.
🖥 The terminal to open inside the GUI tab. If not installed yet it is auto-installed on first GUI start (Konsole, in KDE, has a large initial download — Wi-Fi recommended).
#RRGGBB format. Invalid values are saved with the original color unchanged.

`sshd` can also be launched from the terminal (port comes from sshd_config\'s Port, or `-p`).\nOpenSSH /usr/sbin/sshd breaks privsep under proot → we use dropbear.\nSee docs/SSH-INTO-Z2TERM.md for details
✅ Granted. From the terminal you can `cd /sdcard` to the shared storage.\n `/storage/app` is the app-private area and needs no permission.
Not granted. `cd /sdcard` will look empty. Use the button below to grant all-files\naccess. (`/storage/app` works without permission.)
Wipe the GUI display packages (cache and all) and reinstall (tens to hundreds of MB). Wi-Fi recommended. Continue?
The first GUI (Linux desktop) launch requires display packages to be downloaded (tens to hundreds of MB). Wi-Fi recommended. Continue?
Keeps the terminal session running in the background
While resident servers run, the app stays in the background. Swiping it away from recents will not end the session. You can end it here.
Return the terminal to a freshly opened state. Resident servers keep running.
Stop the resident servers, system event capture and the session, then close the app (like a task kill). Your settings are left alone, so capture resumes the next time you open the app.
Keep any server (sshd/http/smb, …) running in the background — even without opening the app.
No servers yet. Add one with a start command (e.g. python3 -m http.server 8080).
Servers run inside the selected OS. Install the server yourself (sshd/smbd/…); this only runs your start command and restarts it if it exits. Ports below 1024 cannot be bound without root.
Launch enabled servers right after the device boots, without opening the app.
Preset (fills in a start command; edit freely)

When on (and notification access is granted), incoming notifications are detected. Whether they are written to a file is controlled by \"Save notification log\" below. A generic hook — you decide what to filter/serve from the terminal. Fully local.
Write detected notifications to ~/.z2term/notifications.jsonl. When off, notifications are still detected but nothing is written. Repeated re-posts of the same notification are logged only once.
Notification access: not granted (tap below to grant)
Placeholders: {time} {ts} {app} {pkg} {title} {text} {category} {key}. One-line: {text1} {title1}. Escapes: \\n \\t. Applies to new entries.
Insert each new entry at the head of the file (prepend) instead of appending at the end.
⚠ This log has grown to %1$s MB

While "Newest at the top" is ON, the whole file is read and rewritten for every single entry. As it keeps growing this gets slow, and eventually entries can no longer be recorded. Turn this off (append at the end) or trim the file from the terminal.
Command to empty it (tap to copy)
Command to read it (tap to copy)

When on (and the SMS permission is granted), incoming SMS are written to ~/.z2term/sms.jsonl. Unlike notifications, SMS bodies are not redacted by Android\'s sensitive-notification protection and work even while locked — so one-time passwords come through reliably. A generic hook; you decide what to extract from the terminal. Fully local.
SMS permission: not granted (tap below to grant)
Placeholders: {time} {ts} {from} {body}. One-line: {body1}. Escapes: \\n \\t. Applies to new entries. Log: ~/.z2term/sms.jsonl
Could not add a device admin on this device (it may be blocked by device policy)

When on, a background service logs screen on/off, unlock, charging, battery low/okay and Wi-Fi connect/disconnect to ~/.z2term/events.jsonl. A generic automation hook — you decide what to do from the terminal. Fully local. Shows an ongoing notification while active.
Placeholders: {time} {ts} {event} {level} {ssid}. Escapes: \\n \\t. Empty = JSONL. SSID needs location permission and may be blank. Applies to new entries.

When on (and device admin is active), failed and successful lock-screen unlocks are logged to ~/.z2term/events.jsonl as unlock_failed / unlock_succeeded ({level} = consecutive failure count). An anti-theft detection hook — you decide the action (notify, record location, sound an alarm) from a macro. No photo or upload is built in. Fully local.
Device admin: not active — activate it to receive unlock events
Used only to detect lock-screen unlock failures for your anti-theft macros. This app does not lock, wipe, or reset your device.
Needs device admin (watch-login only; no remote lock/wipe). Events: unlock_failed with {level}=failure count, unlock_succeeded. Build your reaction as a macro on events.jsonl.
Could not start logging (check the destination folder)
Konsole does not run on Alpine

On Alpine, Konsole crashes while it builds its window, so the GUI tab would stay black with no explanation. Switch the GUI terminal to xterm and open Alpine? xterm, rxvt-unicode and LXTerminal all work on Alpine — you can pick another one later in Settings.
Alpine is the OS in use, and Konsole crashes there while it builds its window. Pick a different GUI terminal (xterm, rxvt-unicode or LXTerminal), or switch to another OS first.
No learning history yet. Entries are recorded when you confirm a conversion in the Japanese keyboard.
Clear all learning history? This cannot be undone.
Notifications posted by z2-notify from the terminal.
Heads-up notifications from z2-notify -h (pops up at the top of the screen).
Keeps writing what appears on screen to a text file
Starts recording as soon as a tab connects, so nothing is lost when you forget to press ⚪. Applies to tabs opened from now on
Copy a command to open it in the terminal
Relative to home (~). Reachable from the terminal and from file managers
yyyy=year MM=month dd=day HH=hour mm=minute ss=second
When starting, write what was already on screen (and in the scrollback) first
Append if the name already exists
Off = a new file every time (-2, -3 … are added on a name clash)
Apps that redraw the whole screen. Best left off — it does not come out as readable text
Raw log for bug reports. Off converts it to human-readable text
Prefixes each line with a fixed-width date and time, like [2026-07-27 08:42:13]. Not applied to raw logs, which must stay byte-for-byte
Replaces name=value pairs such as TOKEN=…, pasted private keys, and fixed-shape tokens like ghp_ / AKIA with [z2term:masked]

Note: whatever appears on screen goes in as-is (a password you only type never appears on screen, so it is not recorded). The toolbar button stays lit while recording.\nNote: masking only covers clearly recognisable shapes and is not complete — a secret in your own format goes straight through. Always read a log before handing it to someone.
Shows the ssh address, resident servers, automation rules and battery, and runs your macros in the background with one tap.
No macros yet. Run z2-macro install all in the terminal.
Up to %1$d. A tap runs the macro in the background \u2014 the app does not open. Tap a running macro again to stop it.
To add more: put your own .sh in ~/.z2term/macros/ in the terminal, or run z2-macro install all. Then reopen this screen.
Shows the start or the end of a file on your home screen — macro output, events.jsonl, session logs. Like head or tail, without opening the app.
Tap ⚙ and choose a file to watch.
That file does not exist yet.
This file appears on the home screen. Type a path, or tap through the folders below. The number of lines follows the widget\'s height.
Larger text is easier to read but fits fewer lines.
for a log that keeps growing
That path is not a file, so it cannot be saved.
~/.z2term/macros is empty. Run z2-macro install all in the terminal, then add the widget again.
The ✓ marks and times on the buttons clear on their own when the day changes. This clears them now. Your macros are not touched.
While on, no rule runs when its trigger fires. Rules are not deleted, and you can still try one yourself with ▶.
■ Paused: triggers will not run anything
No rules yet. Tap + New to make one, or use z2-when in the terminal (e.g. z2-when charge:start run ~/.z2term/macros/backup.sh).
Name (optional — the trigger is shown when empty)
Pick a trigger (inserts a ready-to-run form)
if = device state at that moment
cooldown = do not run again for this long
between = only in this time window
Unknown trigger: %1$s (pick one from the list below)
Malformed trigger: %1$s (pick one from the list below)
Keep the command on one line (a line break cuts it short).
Line breaks were turned into spaces (a rule reads one line only).
Shown for reference. Edit it in the terminal.

▶ = run once without waiting for the trigger / ▤ = that rule\'s run log / ✎ = edit / ✕ = delete. Rules made with z2-when in the terminal can be edited here too — the source of truth is the text under ~/.z2term/when/.
Review your rules, toggle them, read their logs, try one, or pause them all at once.

Offer the built-in keyboard to the rest of the system, so the same keyboard and the same Japanese conversion work in the app\'s own text fields (snippets, SSH, SFTP, settings) and in other apps. Turn it on in the OS list first, then pick it with the keyboard switcher.
Turn it on in Android settings
The terminal itself is unaffected: it keeps using the keyboard drawn inside the app.
Copied text shows up here.\nCopy first, then open the keyboard.
Emoji you use show up here.\nPick one from the tabs on the right.
off — tap to keep the screen on
Tile %1$d has nothing on it. Assign one in the terminal, e.g. z2-tile set %1$d backup.sh

Stop the screen turning off by itself, for as long as you say. This is the OS-wide setting, so it holds with the app in the background — unlike the toolbar\'s 🔅, which only lasts while the app is on screen. The original value is always written back at the deadline.
Modify system settings: not allowed (tap below to allow)
In the terminal (tap to copy). z2-screen keepon off puts it back early

z2help for the full list / z2doctor when something does not work

It will show next time you open the app

The bundled sample macros. Pick one to put the steps for it on cards above the terminal. Tapping a card runs that one line (steps that need a value of your own ask first); ✕ drops the ones you do not need.
Tap to run (Ctrl-C first, so a half-typed line cannot mix in) / ✕ to skip a step

Bundles settings, SSH connections, snippets, automation rules and macros into one file. The OS image (hundreds of MB) is not included — what a reinstall restores is kept separate from what would be lost forever.
Writes settings, SSH connections, snippets, automation rules and macros to a single file. You choose where to save it next.
